answers.answer: Roll one die per held office card simultaneously; add one per fatigue and one more for Chairman. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire the officeholder to Pensioners, flip the card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply.

Players who retired at least one pensioner may take or discard one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. Ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from PM. Do not replace cards while selecting; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players. After selection discard all remaining cards and refill exactly three (prestige faceup, blackmail facedown), even if nobody took one. Return unused pensioners to supply.

The marker position at phase start determines whether the player may take that main family action twice; move it to the chosen main action after resolving it. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action, which is not doubled and does not move the marker. With at least four vacant offices, Enlist Writer gets one additional writer once this turn; doubled writer action therefore places three total.

After family actions, while Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant into Court, making it a Company share, and lower Debt by one; repeat. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible preserving order. Initial Seek Share payments go to the bank, not Company treasuries.
answers.evidence: “New Company shares” and Seek Share row.

answers.answer: Fill vacant offices in ascending number on card backs. The designated hirer chooses an eligible candidate. Hiring your own family into an ordinary office requires verbal consent from every other player represented in that office’s candidate pool; Chairman election and Commander appointments are exempt. When promoting an officeholder, move their fatigue to the new card and put the old card into vacancies in ascending order. If there is no candidate or hirer, skip the office; it stays vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

The former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. If no candidate gets support, the former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including self, without Nepotism consent. If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, using a supply member or, if needed and possible, a prize member and losing that prize’s VP; if impossible there is no Chairman. The winner’s share moves to Chairman slot but still counts as a Company share for dividends, majority, and scoring; it cannot be traded or invested in firms.

Commit resources and pay all check cash from the acting office treasury to the bank; gather dice, subtract penalties, roll, and use the lowest die. 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and can retry if resources and office limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic, ends that office’s actions, returns its holder to supply, discards fatigue, and flips its card to Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm rules can modify this. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success (examples: trade with no ship, or Deploy without dice to trigger officer losses).

Chairman may add up to three Debt freely, each adding £5 to Balance. Each additional advance requires consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares (Chairman counts); do not pass the Debt track end. Chairman must allocate all Balance to other offices’ treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer, and may interleave borrowing and allocation while respecting borrowing rules. Cash already in offices remains there.

Shipping must spend its treasury until £2 or less remains. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. Place each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once it exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh.

President declares regions including its home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 of its treasury buys a die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. On success fill one order per ship in its sea zone, as possible within declared regions, starting with a writer in home port and then adjacent orders; use actual writers before filled tokens. No President may fill another President’s home region, even if vacant. For each order add its printed revenue to Balance, or half rounded down if a firm already filled it this turn; President gets £1 per order and writer owners £1 per writer. One successful Trade maximum per President per turn; failed attempts can retry during the same uninterrupted opportunity if affordable. The summary gives no separate rule for a protected “home region” beyond home port inclusion and the no-other-President-home restriction.

Deploy may target the Commander’s own Presidency home, any associated region, or a region bordering an associated region; not another home or another Presidency’s Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order for the action to have effect. Exhaust officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice, then subtract strength of target and all other regions in its empire (target counted once); Company-controlled defense strength is zero. After every attempt, each owner rolls one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments make no officer-loss rolls.

On successful Deploy, loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, with minimum equal to surviving officers used in that attempt plus one. Repeated payout cycles pay £1 to Commander family for Commander plus each of its used surviving officers, then clockwise £1 per other family’s used surviving officers, then bank £1 per used regiment and local-alliance piece; repeat until loot is distributed. Commander gets one trophy per target tower. Then remove target tower and dome (if capital, all matching flags), open all its orders and remove unrest; if newly Company controlled, set control token region-side up, place Governor overlay on map and office card in vacancies (unless Governor General is in play). Move outward-facing Elephant fully inside target. On catastrophe, Commander returns half own family’s trophies rounded up and member to supply; exhausted officers still check losses.

Governor takes printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls current pool without penalty, then reduces pool by one regardless of result. Success earns £1, or £2 if immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose one: build a ship (first success places partial ship in region, a later success completes it into associated President’s sea zone); commission a regiment into that President’s Army; or tax an unsplit £2 to Balance or that President’s treasury. Any unsuccessful roll adds unrest; catastrophe also removes officeholder. Each Tax after the first this turn adds unrest. May repeat until stopping, no dice remain, or catastrophe.

Company expenses are £1 per Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army, and each ship in a sea zone including China; exclude Commanders. If Balance is insufficient, take £5 emergency loans, advancing Debt one each until track end, then continue taking loans even at maximum Debt; new debt adds no current-turn expense. Set Balance to zero after loans. One or two loans lower Standing one; three or more lower it two. Then check remaining Balance against expectations under current Standing and lower Standing one if short. Dividends are checked after expectations: Chairman may pay affordable dividends at £1 per share to each owner; if total cash paid is strictly greater than expectations, Standing rises one.

Crisis resolves at Elephant’s location, tail attacking head, then Elephant March. For Company attacks, resolve primary first, then secondary rebellions in every other unrest Company region, in Bombay, Madras, Bengal order; each Commander orders attacks within their Presidency. Primary normal Crisis strength is ordinary Invasion/Rebellion strength plus unrest in target; secondary attack strength is only unrest cubes there. A Commander exhausts active Army pieces totaling strength or as much as possible; local alliances count printed strength and cannot split. The stated defense succeeds only if newly exhausted pieces equal Crisis strength; a matched defense removes all unrest and gives Commander a trophy, and if it defeated a normal primary Invasion also removes one attacker tower if possible. If Commander vacant, Military Affairs acts, or Chairman if that office is vacant; acting player chooses pieces and receives/loses no trophies. Exact handling of an indivisible alliance exceeding required strength is explicitly unresolved.
answers.evidence: “Crisis,” especially “Attacks on Company”; FAQ source gap.

answers.answer: A law fails at support −1 or less: discard law, resolve dilemma’s If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial, new PM shifts proposed policy one space either direction and resolves that adjacent policy. A law passes at zero or higher: keep as passed, PM takes passed-law token, resolve selected policy then immediate law effects. On pass, restore all voting cards afterward either way. A dilemma forces selection and ends law drawing; there is no special support-zero exception stated (zero passes).

In 1758 and Long 1710, at turn start before London Season, PM may call Deregulation if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call it if either is on a starred space. It uses ordinary voting procedure and support threshold, with exceptions: passing lowers Debt one per two current Debt, sets Standing to S, gives PM a passed-law token, and activates firms; failure increases Company share scoring value by flipping/placing Court VP token up to ±3. There is no policy; failure neither removes PM nor discards Deregulation law, and PM may vote against. 1813 begins deregulated.

To form a firm, only a player managing none may return an eligible Company share to supply or flip a workshop to invested side; place a family member as first firm share, set Value to leftmost, and take £5 from bank into London treasury. To invest in an existing firm, obtain manager consent and contribute a Company share or workshop in the same manner, creating one share and £5 London cash. Company shares are prohibited when Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space; Chairman share and shares created this turn (even traded away) cannot be used. Up to ten shares; further investments still add £5 but create no shares. Invested workshops never revert and do not earn workshop bonus or Company-failure VP even if firm fails.

Each firm gets exactly one trade attempt per turn. Managers secretly and simultaneously choose a trade zone/home port (requires ship, may be closed at selection) and London-treasury bid, or Hobnob (no bid/trade/dividends). Reveal bids simultaneously; strategy stays hidden until its Presidency begins. At start of matching Presidency operations, firms reveal and roll one die per £1 bid, paying bid to bank; any 1/2 permits trade. Initiative is ship count minus successful bid dice. Successful President Trade also generates initiative; fill in lowest initiative order, ties chosen by President, or Chairman if President vacant/never succeeds (firms then fill after Commander/Governor chances). Each firm fills open orders up to ships+1 starting at home port, tracing its route; once per order for that firm. Revenue goes to India treasury; may refill orders others filled that turn for half listed revenue rounded down. Advance Value one per full £6 added to India treasury.

At start of Revenue before Company, firms pay expenses in initiative order then other firms; ties by manager with most windows then PM clockwise. Cost is £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or Value, paid from either/both treasuries. An unpaid firm dissolves unless rescued by emergency investments (normal share/workshop rules, even beyond ten-share limit; pay expenses, lose remaining cash, lower Value one per rescue investment) or by merging with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if needed and cover the shortfall. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships to shipyards, charter to family side; invested workshops stay invested. After expenses, manager may pay dividends from India treasury only: £1 per share plus £1 manager per dividend; consenting shareholders may forgo their share payouts. Record total actual payout; active firm paying none records zero, Hobnob retains prior marker; remaining India cash sweeps to London.

Limited components include pieces and tokens generally; when a supply runs out, complete as much as possible. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited. Public information includes all information, discards and family cash; facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection are hidden.

Negotiations may trade enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Cannot trade officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, or PM dial; Chairman piece cannot transfer. When share transfers, replace its member with new owner’s family piece. Blackmail can be shown privately but not traded faceup; once used it is faceup and no longer tradable.

Immediate transfers are binding; future-behavior promises are not, except promise cards can force their guaranteed effect if possible, subject to card timing/limits. Promises may be traded to a third party or guarantor. If multiple calls cannot all be fulfilled simultaneously, guarantor chooses which to fulfill. No promises may be called during Final Scoring. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (example: workshop bonus already paid this Bonuses phase does not trigger again after sale that phase).

For five players add three extra player setup cards; for six add six. Shuffle and deal evenly; take holdings listed on the dealt cards, including cash, enterprises and positions. Each starting luxury grants 2 VP. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together and deal three display cards with prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.

Game ends after scenario final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Failure is immediate normally; if during Events in India finish that phase, and if legislation causes failure finish the vote before scoring. Once game over, stop negotiations, calling promises, and playing blackmail unless a card explicitly permits Final Scoring use.

Final Power is enterprise/share Power from track (bottom two spaces zero), plus one per passed-law token and trophy, two for PM, and printed card power including blackmail and applicable spouse. First/second awards by final turn are 3/1 on turns 1–3, 5/2 on 4–6, 8/4 on 7–8. Tied first players each receive only the lower award and nobody gets the other award; tied second get none. Overall victory tie: most windows, then clockwise from PM.

If Company survives, Company shares score Court’s current VP each and final survival procedure rolls office attrition and retires pensioners without prestige cards. If it fails, each Company share loses Court’s current VP and each uninvested workshop gives +1 VP; resolve one random failure card instead of normal survival procedure. Deregulated firm shares are scored first and eligible special retirements occur whether Company survives or fails.

Spouses cannot be transferred and impose permanent restrictions; required enterprise/share trades occur immediately when gained. Retirement discounts are personal, may stack, and each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. Discounts reduce actual retirement spending and therefore prestige-selection priority.
If Violet Effingham returns shipyards, fitted ships remain in play; those shipyards cannot be purchased while their ships remain in play.

Enlist Writer: no cost stated; place a family member in any Presidency Writers box, with one additional writer once this turn if at least four offices are vacant. Enlist Officer: no cost stated; place member in Officers-in-Training. Purchase Luxury: £4 to bank; take luxury, worth 2 VP while owned and one window icon (social). Purchase Shipyard: £2 to bank; take shipyard and matching ship, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted (shipping). Purchase Workshop: £5 to bank; take workshop, two votes and £1 bonus; if Company fails it is worth 1 VP unless invested (manufacturing). Seek Share: pay bank according to empty queue space (£2, £3, £3, £4, £5), place member as applicant; after family actions it may become a Court share and reduce Debt.

If a family must place a piece but has none in supply, take one from any of its prizes and lose that prize’s printed VP; applies to firm-share creation too. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns, using a supply piece or, if necessary and possible, a prize piece and losing its VP; if impossible, there is no Chairman. Summary does not specify a distinct rule for lack of both supply pieces and prizes beyond that impossibility condition.

Chairman hires Director (eligible current officeholder except Chairman/Governor; if all offices vacant, any writer), Shipping (any writer), Military Affairs (Presidential Commander, else officer, else trainee), and China (any writer). Director hires Presidents (writer or Governor associated with Presidency); associated President hires Governor (writer or officer in region; Commander ineligible). Governor General replaces Director and is hired same way. If no candidate or hirer exists, office is skipped and remains vacant, taking no actions including hiring.
answers.evidence: “Nepotism and its exceptions” office table and “Hiring.”

answers.answer: Successful Special Envoy opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing Superintendent overlay/card and immediately having Chairman hire any writer. Director may repeat Envoy checks, paying £1 treasury per die without penalty. After all Envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each moving one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones, including China once created; no transfers while still taking Envoys.

Military Affairs first may make up to two transfers of one officer or regiment between Armies, keeping it in top half; next assigns every trainee to any Army’s top half; finally appoints Commanders. If a vacancy or a family has more total pieces in an Army than current Commander’s family, choose from families with most pieces; move chosen officer to Commander slot and previous Commander to top as officer. A tie with incumbent’s family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; each position gets an opportunity, but Commanders/Governors may decline. Each position completes all its actions before next, so another cannot interrupt a position’s retries; Trade may be placed before/after them. If President vacant, Chairman sets order only and cannot Trade or approve local alliance purchases.

Trade ships do not exhaust under the described rules. On Refresh, return writers to associated Presidencies, return filled tokens and Presidency dividers, return extra ships to supply, reactivate exhausted officers/regiments, and exhaust any active local alliances. Fitted player ships retain fatigue.
answers.evidence: “Upkeep and Refresh” says what returns/exhausts; no separate trade-ship exhaustion is stated.

answers.answer: Commander first requests Presidency treasury money for local alliances at printed cost; President must approve purchase and alliances move to top. Each alliance’s printed strength can be used once that turn, either for Deploy or defense, and cannot be split between purposes.

General Deploy has no additional dice penalty stated for targeting a Company region; Company defense strength is zero. It must have unrest or a closed order to have an effect. Success loot is £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, with minimum equal to surviving officers in that attempt plus one; Commander receives one trophy per target tower. The summary does not give a distinct exception for deploying solely to reopen orders or clear unrest, so whether that purpose changes penalty, minimum loot, or trophies is not established.
answers.evidence: “Commanders and Deploy”; the requested special-purpose ruling is not specified.

answers.answer: A Governor needs two successful Build options total: first successful build puts a partial ship in the Governor’s region; a later successful build completes it into that Governor’s President-associated sea zone. A commissioned regiment goes into the Army associated with that President; it has officer-like strength, loot is paid to bank, and it causes no officer-loss rolls.

China is created by successful Special Envoy or Envoy to China law. After Envoy it is immediately hired by Chairman choosing any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash; Shipping and Director may send ships to it, and they count as Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. China acts after Bengal and may attempt Trade once then; its ships count for its dice.
answers.evidence: “Director of Trade” and “Superintendent of Trade in China.”

answers.answer: China may make only one Trade attempt per turn, so a failed check is not repeated that turn. It requires at least one export icon among Company regions and rolls one die per ship. On success add £4 to Balance and £1 per export icon across Company-controlled regions to Superintendent; non-Company-region export icons do not count toward that bonus.
answers.evidence: “Superintendent of Trade in China”: may attempt Trade once; success bonus counts icons across Company-controlled regions.

answers.answer: Passing Governor General law makes all Governors pensioners, removes their overlays and partial Company ships, returns Governor/Director cards to box, replaces Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue, and places ribbon overlay. No Governors/overlays are created on future conquests; printed Company symbols indicate control. Governor General hires Presidents and uses Director treasury/turn position. Skip Governor Elimination when regions are lost.

Before Govern checks, Governor General adds £3 to Balance per Company region. It may repeatedly attempt Govern, paying £1 treasury per die without penalty, but can have at most one successful Govern per turn. Every rolled 6 adds one unrest in each Company region, even on success; failure adds another unrest in every Company region. Success adds £1 per Company region and requires one benefit per region: complete a Company ship into any sea zone including China, place regiment in any Army, or add £2 to Balance/any other office treasury (not own) and add unrest to a Company region. Tax unrests from multiple choices must go to different regions.

For player ships in storm zone, roll once each: 1–2 no effect; 3–4 fatigue if fresh or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Sunk ship returns to shipyard unfatigued. Company and extra ships are storm-exempt. China ships count Eastern. Firm ships face storms in their chosen strategy zone; Hobnob firms are exempt.

When an order newly closes, return any writer there to owner’s supply; flip a filled token to closed. If told to close an order in a region whose orders are already all closed, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to that region’s orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region’s northernmost open order; if none, it Cascades too. A region can initiate a Cascade once per event tile but can receive multiple Cascade effects.

For Turmoil, close northernmost open order in region on back of new top draw-stack tile; if all closed, Cascade. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in that region and every bordering region. Shuffle moves Elephant, shuffles that tile into remaining draw stack, separately shuffles discards and places them on top; if draw stack is empty, March last instead.

If Leader’s top-stack region is sovereign, it gains one tower. If dominated, it rebels with printed explosion modifier. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

Peace opens orders connected across Elephant’s border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. If Elephant is wholly inside a region instead, open all its orders and remove its unrest. Then Elephant Marches.

For non-Company Invasion Crisis, compare attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier against defender’s whole empire strength; attacker must be strictly greater. On success replace defender flag with attacker dominated flag; taking capital shatters its whole empire. If attacker had no empire, use free capital/star and matching small flag; if none available, no new empire/flags form. Failure costs attacker one tower.

For non-Company Rebellion compare only rebelling region strength plus modifier to its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions do not count. Rebel must be strictly greater; a tie therefore fails. On success actor becomes sovereign and removes its flag, closing its orders (Cascade if already closed); on failure remove one tower from capital.

On Region Loss, Commander returns half family trophies rounded up and member to supply; roll one die per officer in associated Army, each 6 removes officer. Eliminate Governor: return office card to unused stack and fatigue/member to supply; remove Governor overlay, partial ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion’s specified strength) and appropriate invasion flag. Return control token to region loot-side down, so future conquest has no loot modifier and region loses Presidency association. Invasion Crisis closes all orders (or Cascades if already closed); Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing drops by number of regions lost so far this turn (first −1, second additional −2, etc.). The summary does not say these losses automatically remove other Company regions.

After successful Invasion Crisis, Elephant moves to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); otherwise March targets the top-stack region. It is placed fully inside a Company region, points toward sovereign from dominated region, or in a sovereign region points across shape-marked border on tile. If neighbor already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not so dominated; if all neighbors are dominated, follow redirect-arrow shape toward empire capital.

Foreign Invasion uses storm die to select target Presidencies: West Bombay, South Madras, East Bengal; all storms selects each, no storms selects top-stack region. For each target roll ordinary die for attack strength and resolve Invasion/Company attack. On success close all orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set towers to half attack roll rounded down. If Elephant was fully inside an invaded Company region, March with circle shape only. Unrest does not add to primary attack or tower strength (designer ruling); event still uses Company-defense procedure and secondary unrest attacks.

PM reveals up to three laws one at a time and chooses one, discarding others; drawing a dilemma forces selection and ends drawing. PM then chooses direction around dial, stopping at first matching policy space. The summary does not state a general rule allowing PM to stop drawing early except the dilemma condition, nor further policy-selection restrictions.

Tax pays bank £1 per owned target; unpaid target returns to supply, including Chairman if taxed. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each family member’s prize; return enterprise/prize member if unable. Bonus pays bank £1 per owned target. Power swaps target marker with next higher marker; if target already highest, swap any other pair.

Starting with PM and proceeding clockwise, players cast votes; each £1 family cash buys one vote plus printed card votes (rotate used cards). Adjust support up/down. After each full round PM may call another or stop; a round with no votes ends voting. Restore used voting cards to normal orientation after resolution.
answers.evidence: “Voting”; summary does not give a special rule governing reuse of prior votes across rounds.

answers.answer: A player who voted for may later oppose; after opposing they cannot vote for during that vote. Track opposition totals; biggest opponent holds Opposition Leader, with tied current holder retaining it. With recipient consent, votes can be cast on behalf of someone already opposed or committing to oppose, adding to that person’s opposition total. PM cannot oppose or consent to opposing enterprises except forced “Vote with my enterprises” promise.

On final turn, still pay upkeep for every prize; if unable, return member and lose printed VP, then skip Refresh and go to Final Scoring. On nonfinal turns, after upkeep return writers to associated Presidencies, filled tokens and dividers, extra ships to supply; reactivate exhausted officers/regiments, exhaust any active local alliances, advance turn. Fitted player ships keep fatigue.

Each shareholder may make one extra retirement per London Season from supply rather than Pensioners, irrespective of firms owned, but spending cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker among firms where they hold shares; cannot retire from a firm with absent or zero marker. Spouse discounts can enable a higher printed-cost prize; otherwise normal retirement rules apply, including prestige eligibility. At start Final Scoring, score firms then each shareholder may make one special retirement regardless of Company survival/failure, before normal final-scoring steps; no display cards then.

Firm investment cash (£5 per contribution) goes from bank to London treasury; trade proceeds go to India treasury. London funds ship fitting (bank), trade bids (bank), and can pay expenses; India can pay expenses and dividends, then remaining India cash sweeps to London. Buying an already Company-fitted player ship pays Shipping treasury (£3 unfatigued, £2 fatigued) with owner consent. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.

Firms phase is after Family share creation and before Hiring, only if deregulated. Investments happen in no set order until nobody wants more, then strategies are chosen. Firm manager resolves timing conflicts within own firm; PM resolves conflicts between firms.

Firm may fit ship from shipyard for £3 from London with owner consent. It may buy player-owned ship already in Company with owner consent, paying Shipping treasury £3 if unfatigued or £2 fatigued. It cannot acquire Company or extra ships. Summary gives no special authorization to buy another player’s ship without consent; the stated purchase requires consent.

Hostile takeover requires you not to manage target and consent from holders of a majority of its shares. Move target ships, money and shares to your charter and copy both cube positions; former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

Merger requires managers to negotiate with every shareholder’s consent. Highest-Value firm is primary; if tied, players choose among tied firms. Transfer all secondary shares, ships, and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides. Negotiate any transfers and return of over-ten shares with those owners’ consent. It is one binding immediate transfer; primary’s Value/dividend track remains.
Hobnob means no bid, trade, or dividends, but firm still pays expenses and retains prior dividend marker for retirement. Firm ships are exempt from storms while Hobnobbing.
answers.evidence: “Firm strategies” and “Firm expenses, rescue and dividends.”

answers.answer: Yes, emergency investment can rescue a firm even at ten shares. Follow normal Company-share/workshop contribution rules; the ten-share cap means further investment creates no share but still contributes £5. Pay expenses, lose remaining cash, and lower Value one space per emergency investment. Same-turn Company share restriction still applies (shares created this turn cannot be contributed even after trade); other restrictions remain.
answers.evidence: “Firm expenses, rescue and dividends” and “Firms phase: investments.”

answers.answer: Emergency rescue may merge the endangered firm with only one other firm, rather than a normal negotiated multi-firm merger. The rescuing firm must first pay its own expenses if not already paid, then cover endangered firm unpaid expenses.

Voluntary dissolution requires consent of all shareholders. Apply the dissolution destinations: firm shares go to Debtor’s Prison (−1 VP each), ships return to shipyards, and the charter returns to family side. Invested workshops do not recover to uninvested state; they remain invested even if the firm fails.
answers.evidence: “Voluntary dissolution” refers to dissolution destinations; “Firm expenses, rescue and dividends” specifies shares, ships, charter, and workshops.

answers.answer: If deregulated, score each firm share at firm’s printed Value VP, add fractional values across shares before rounding down, and deduct 1 VP per family piece in Debtor’s Prison; do this before normal final scoring and special retirement. Value 1=−1, 2=0, 3–4=½, 5–7=1, 8–9=1½, 10=2 VP per share. This scoring applies before Company survival/failure scoring, and special retirement follows even if Company failed.
The five prizes each cost/upkeep/VP/windows: £2/£0/0/0; £4/£1/2/1; £8/£2/4/2; £14/£3/8/3; £20/£4/12/4. Summary does not specify which turn windows apply; prize window tax is referenced generally.
answers.evidence: “Prizes” table; windows timing not detailed there.

answers.answer: 1710 starts turn 1 and ends turn 5, with no deregulation procedures. 1758 starts turn 3 and ends turn 7, with Deregulation available. 1813 starts turn 5 and ends turn 8, and begins deregulated. Long 1710 starts turn 1 and ends turn 8, with Deregulation available.

1710: Standing £10 expectations, Debt 0, each office treasury £3, Royal Protection law, one regiment per Army, no Company ships. 1758: Standing £12 expectations, Debt 3, each office treasury £4, Calico Acts, one regiment per Army, one Company ship in East Indian, and Bengal control token in Bengal Presidency.

1813 starts Standing £10, Debt 0, treasuries £3 each; laws Military Oversight, Deregulation (Debtor’s Prison side), Calico Acts; two regiments per Army; one Company ship per sea zone. Setup additionally places +2/−2 share-value token in Court, creates China, puts Bombay/Madras/Bengal control tokens in their Presidencies, returns Governor General law to box and places its office overlay over Director of Trade; use Governor General instead of Director and no Governors. Exact map configuration comes from scenario card reverse, not specified in summary.

For final turns 1–3 awards are 3 VP first and 1 second; turns 4–6 are 5/2; turns 7–8 are 8/4. If first place is tied, each tied player gets only the lower (second-place) award and no one gets the other award.

Initial Power: Social 2, Company shares 1, Shipping 0, Manufacturing 0. Standing expectations spaces are £4/6/8/10/12/14/16; reset S is above £10. Deregulation is permitted at Standing £4/6/8 or Debt 5/6/7/8 (lined); mandatory if Standing £4 or Debt 8 (starred). Summary does not name a location/meaning for “S” beyond reset S.

Unrest does not increase a Foreign Invasion primary attack or determine resulting tower strength. Use ordinary attack die for attack and halve it, rounding down, for tower level. Event still uses Company-defense procedure and its secondary unrest attacks; do not apply normal primary Crisis added unrest. Orders are closed on success; if already all closed, Cascade.
answers.evidence: FAQ “Foreign Invasion and unrest” and event procedure.

answers.answer: Mercantile/Diplomatic Connection: if it reduces a check to zero dice, that is failure. Company Fraud occurs at start of Revenue; roll one die per your officeholder, reduce Balance by twice highest roll (minimum zero), and receive only the cash actually removed from Balance. Public Demands Impeachment returns member to supply and office card to vacancies. Military Oversight’s demoted Commander is eligible as an officer for reappointment.
answers.evidence: FAQ “Applicable official errata” and “Company Fraud payout cap.”

answers.answer: Shared setup: initial Company Balance £5; family VP markers start at zero; put local alliances in their named Army boxes and loot tokens money-side up in matching regions. For the chosen scenario, use its setup card for map and other scenario-specific position; set Turn marker to its date and PM dial to matching date. Summary does not specify a separate procedure for setting a Prime Minister “arm” beyond pointing the PM dial to matching date.

Normal order: London Season → Family → Firms if deregulated → Hiring → Company Operation → Bonuses → Revenue → Events in India → Parliament Meets → Upkeep and Refresh. Special Deregulation vote is at turn start before London Season. Skip London Season on the game’s first turn. Firms follows Deregulation when that vote activates firms, and occupies the Firms phase position after Family and before Hiring.

Retirements start with Chairman, or former Chairman if office vacant, then clockwise. Each player may retire each pensioner to a prize; the summary does not say retirement is mandatory. Pay printed cost, move member to prize and gain VP; set actual spending aside until London Season ends to establish display order, then pay bank. Unused pensioners return to their supplies at end of display step.

Summary says an empire capital flag is removed if only the capital remains. It does not say whether losing the last dominated region while capital remains triggers removal, or whether the procedure differs between Rebellion and Company conquest; that distinction is unsupported by this summary.
answers.evidence: “India terminology” states the capital-flag rule generally but not the asked loss-specific cause.

answers.answer: Firm share VP at Value: 1=−1; 2=0; 3=½; 4=½; 5=1; 6=1; 7=1; 8=1½; 9=1½; 10=2. Sum fractional points across shares before rounding down at scoring.
answers.evidence: “Firm-track VP per share” in Scoring / Victory Conditions.
